content: Yes, that is correct. In Swiss referendums, each of the 26 cantons is allocated one vote, regardless of its population size. For a proposal to be accepted, it must meet two criteria: a simple majority of all voters nationwide must vote in favor, and a simple majority of the cantons (i.e., at least 13 out of 26) must also vote in favor. This dual-majority requirement is a unique feature of Swiss direct democracy.
